overview: White takes a broad centre with c4, d4 and e4, and Black, without having committed the g8-knight, undermines it with ...c6, ...Nd7 and ...e5, or ...c5. Positions often resemble a King's Indian or Pirc with the knight still on g8. White has more space and Black has to find counterplay against it.

white_ideas.idea: Play Nf3, Be2 and castle with a big centre, then Be3 and Qd2 or a space-gaining push
Keep pieces coordinated so the centre is not undermined, aiming for an edge in space

black_ideas.idea: Fianchettoed bishop on g7 and a delayed ...Nf6 or ...Ne7; hit the centre with ...c5 or ...e5
...c6 and ...Qb6 or ...Nd7 and ...e5 for a King's Indian-style structure

typical_structures.structure: White e4/d4/c4 centre against ...d6/...g6 fianchetto; becomes King's Indian or Maroczy type depending on ...e5 or ...c5

character.notes: Black's setup is resilient but passive; White has space. Not forcing, not high-risk for either side.

soundness.notes: Considered sound, with a small risk of passivity.

structure.notes: The big centre may be locked after ...e5 and d5, or attacked with ...c5; undecided at move four.

approach.notes: Modern setup (...g6, ...Bg7, ...d6) can be played against almost any White set-up.

level.notes: Black's plans need judgement about when to break the centre; theory is light.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4...e5
sublines_that_differ.how: King's Indian-type play with ...Ngf6 to follow.

character.reason: Resilient but not extremely hard to break down, and not forcing.

soundness.reason: A legitimate if slightly passive set-up.

structure.reason: White's centre is up against ...e5 or ...c5 and has not yet been fixed.

approach.reason: The Modern setup is played against almost any White set-up.

level.reason: Plans take understanding but there is little theory.

plans.reason: Black lets White take space, then attacks the centre from the g7 bishop and pawn breaks.
